data.why: The addition of 300 new delivery sites for Walmart is a massive, concrete operational expansion that directly impacts the finance back-office. It creates a highly specific, logical opening to discuss the surge in supplier invoices and audit workload.
data.angle: Building 300 new physical locations requires onboarding numerous local suppliers and processing a high volume of invoices, which strains existing AP and audit processes.

not_chosen.reason: Every rep will open with the $1.5B funding round since it was heavily covered. The 300 new sites is a more specific operational trigger for finance.
The CFO transition was over 4 months ago, making it less timely than the recent expansion news.
Headcount growth is a generic trigger compared to the concrete operational challenge of adding 300 new sites.
The Strategic Finance Manager role is relevant, but the 300 new sites provides a stronger, more direct tie to AP and invoice volume.
US manufacturing expansion is a strong hook, but the 300 Walmart sites provides a more concrete number to anchor the message.

data.subject: 300 new sites
data.body:
Hi Sendil,

Saw Zipline is adding 300 new delivery sites for Walmart. Building out that many locations usually means a flood of new supplier invoices to check and approve. Who is auditing all of those today?

Uber Freight cut invoice audit time from 1 day to 1 hour with Zamp.

Open to seeing how?

[Your name]
